stories.title: GLM-5.4: Toward generalized coding with our first loop transformer
stories.reason: Z.ai's GLM-5.4 introduces a 'loop transformer': a 28-layer block run twice with gated blending between passes, built on the GLM-5 base. 1006 HN points/329 comments; commenters estimate ~3x inference compute for a 3x loop. Genuinely new architecture, not a repeat of an already-covered release.
key_facts: 28-layer block looped a fixed 2 iterations with 'Damp Gates' blending old/new state
Built on top of the existing GLM-5 base model, not trained from scratch
1006 HN points, 329 comments; not available via OpenRouter or standard Z.ai API at launch
No official benchmark numbers or parameter count surfaced in the source or discussion

stories.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
stories.reason: DeepMind used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve known quantum algorithms, with every result formally verified in a new open-source Lean library (since the circuits can't be tested on classical or current quantum hardware). Concrete, large speedups across five problems.
key_facts: Inertial confinement fusion: 11.8x lower computing cost, qubits 5650->4338
Cytochrome P450 simulation: 2.5x improvement, qubits 481->333; light-sensitive molecule sim 8x cheaper
Grover's algorithm implementation 2.57x speedup; arcsin loading routine 290x speedup
Lean library, problem specs and verified solutions open-sourced at github.com/google-deepmind/formal-quantum-computation

stories.title: NariQ: BF16-level Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file
stories.reason: NariQ is a trellis-coded (QTIP-style) post-training quantization scheme calibrated on real coding-agent traces. Its own benchmarks show the 3-bit (10.1GB) and 2.5-bit (8.4GB) files matching or beating BF16 (53.8GB) on DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench, AIME and MGSM; 2-bit degrades sharply. Requires a llama.cpp fork, SM120-tuned, self-reported numbers.
key_facts: 3-bit NariQ (10.1GB) beats BF16 (53.8GB) on DeepSWE v1.1 (41.0 vs 39.8) and Terminal-Bench 2.1 (63.8 vs 62.6)
2.5-bit (8.4GB) stays close to BF16; 2-bit (6.8GB) drops sharply (DeepSWE 28.6 vs 39.8)
Requires nari-labs' llama.cpp fork; stock llama.cpp/Ollama/LM Studio can't load the tensor format yet
Self-reported by the authors using the Claude Code harness, not independently verified

stories.title: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation
stories.reason: A detailed, concrete methodology for building agentic evals (HF blog): worked Raman-fitting example showing a shortcut that gamed the original task, benchmark-error stats (28/89 Terminal-Bench tasks corrected, 59.4% of audited SWE-bench Verified problems had issues), and a checklist for publishing evals responsibly. Directly on Mine's always-surface eval-methodology topic.
key_facts: Worked example: unguarded raman-fitting shortcut passed all 8 synthetic tasks by guessing peak widths; fixed by adding per-peak checks
Terminal-Bench 2.1 corrected 28 of 89 tasks after user reports; harness changes alone shifted accuracy up to 29.9 points
Audit found material issues in 59.4% of 138 examined SWE-bench Verified problems; OpenAI estimated ~30% of SWE-Bench Pro tasks broken
~3,500 eval leaderboards and ~17,000 eval datasets on the Hub, roughly 16x growth in eval datasets over the past year

stories.title: AI-Assisted Cyber Attacks Trigger Unauthorized Payments at Indian Banks and Fintech Firms
stories.reason: CERT-In/I4C advisory: attackers made 'multi-crore' unauthorized payments at Indian banks/fintechs by manipulating approval workflows rather than exploiting payment APIs directly, cutting access-to-impact time from days to hours with agentic tooling. Names a specific actor (Crafty Falcon) and its toolset (ARTEX, PentAGI, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI), tying into the earlier Barracuda/EU Commission campaigns.
key_facts: CERT-In: attackers altered approval relationships/business records, then used legitimate payment workflows to move funds via mule accounts (IMPS/NEFT)
Agentic tooling cut time from initial access to impact from days to a few hours
Actor 'Crafty Falcon' linked to tools ARTEX, PentAGI, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI; ARTEX also tied to the Barracuda supply-chain attack (~10 cloud accounts in ~44 hours)
RBI reportedly pressed banks on how they'll keep pace with AI-related threats

stories.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
stories.reason: OpenAI and Cisco's open-source Shirudo uses eBPF to apply temporary, signed 'shields' that block an exploit's specific behavior on a running Linux system while a real patch is prepared, with TPM-backed verification. Demoed live blocking a Java4Shell exploit on a running Elasticsearch process. BSD-2-Clause, concrete mechanism beyond a press release.
key_facts: Mechanism: eBPF programs ('shields') cryptographically signed and TPM-verified, loaded without restart
Codex-generated shield added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder, blocking a live Java4Shell exploit on Elasticsearch
BSD-2-Clause license, BPF programs dual BSD/GPL; GitHub repo, VM quickstart, self-guided lab

stories.title: modelsphere/modelsphere
stories.reason: ModelSphere: an early-stage (196 stars) Apache-2.0 Kubernetes platform for serving LLMs on SGLang/vLLM, with KV-cache/queue-depth-aware autoscaling, latency-based throttling, prefill/decode disaggregation and in-flight generation recovery. Squarely on Mine's favorite topic (how models are served) but small adoption and rough edges in the docs.
key_facts: Autoscales inference replicas on KV-cache pressure and queue depth, not just request rate
Supports NVIDIA and Huawei Ascend hardware; prefill/decode disaggregation with a shared KV cache pool
196 stars, 11 forks, 90 commits, no published releases yet; AutoTune feature labeled preview

stories.title: Localcode, open source agentic coding on your Mac with one command
stories.reason: LocalCode: an Apache-2.0 agentic coding CLI that runs models fully locally on Apple Silicon Macs, with speculative-drafting and 'copy drafting' (3.5-4x faster on files the model already read) speedups and hardware-aware model selection. 162 stars, modest but concrete technical claims.
key_facts: Mac-only (Apple Silicon, 16GB+ unified memory), runs HF models fully locally with an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint
Claims 'copy drafting' is 3.5-4x faster than normal generation when rewriting already-read files; vendor speculative drafters ~2x
162 stars, 6 forks, 879 commits; published on PyPI (uv pip install localcode)
